newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says Burma, Malaysia border woes priority.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says Burma, Malaysia border woes priority.

text.p: Thailand has given top priority to settling its border disputes with neighbours Burma and Malaysia, Foreign Minister Prechuab Chiayasarn said on Thursday.
"The one thing we have to settle as soon as possible are all the border issues," Prechuab told Reuters in an interview.
The biggest problems are those along the 2,400-km (1,440 mile) Thai-Burma border and the illegal movement of mainly South Asian workers into Malaysia from Thailand, Prechuab said.
Relations between Thailand and Burma have been dogged by land and maritime border problems for some time.

The opening of a Friendship Bridge between the southeastern Burmese town of Myawadi and the norwestern Thai town of Mae Sot has been delayed for years by bitter accusations from both sides of encroachment into the river that forms the border.
The last of the overland border crossings between the two countries was closed last year after Burma accused Thailand of letting anti-Rangoon guerrillas cross into Burma to fight.
Prechuab said the two governments were currently involved in negotiations over border demarcations and hoped to settle problems soon in order to reopen the borders.
"It's not our problem, it's their problem. They have to prepare themselves for...outsiders," he said. "We are ready to open but...I think they have to prepare themselves as well."

Prechuab also said the Thai Foreign Ministry had lodged a protest with Burma's ambassador over last week's attack on Karen refugee camps just inside the Thai side of the border in which at least six people died.

Thai troops also repelled Rangoon-backed guerrillas of the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army who tried to enter Thailand from Burma this week as fighting continued between the rival factions of the Karen rebel group.
"We want the Myanmar government to know what is going on. We want them to try to avoid allowing it to happen again," Prechuab said.
Another issue Bangkok hopes to solve quickly is the illegal movement of workers across the Thai border into Malaysia, he added. Most of the workers are from Bangladesh.
Malaysia is cracking down on its growing numbers of illegal workers, and has said it will deport those who did not register for working papers.

Prechuab said not all of the illegal Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia had entered via the border with Thailand, but Bangkok wants to help solve the problem and he had sent people to the southern border to investigate the problem.
"We don't want Malaysia to claim the majority of Bangladeshi workers come from Thailand...some may have come direct. We have to investigate it," he said.

Prechuab said senior officials from the two countries were to discuss the problem next week, and Thailand has proposed a meeting of the two nations as well as representatives of the countries of origin of the workers.
